newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds sigh with relief but must conquer 102.00.
newsitem.headline: Bunds sigh with relief but must conquer 102.00.

text.p: German debt prices joined the post-FOMC party early on Wednesday, pushing higher at the open after the Federal Reserve decided to leave U.S. interest rates on hold.

Traders said the market was staging a relief rally, recapturing some of its losses from the past few sessions, but they said gains were likely to be limited with domestic pressures still weighing on Bunds.
By 0638 GMT, the DTB June future was trading 23 basis points higher on the day at 101.84, having gapped up at the open from Tuesday's high at 101.70.
In the cash market, the 10-year cash Bund was trading at 101.65 for a bid yield of 5.773 percent by the same time.
But Bunds were underperforming Treasuries on spreads with the 10-year yield gap slimming to 101 basis points from 104.

Analysts said the underperformance was partly due to domestic pressure on the German market with political squabbling over how to plug a hole in estimated 1997 tax revenues continuing to concern investors.
The market is expecting M3 money supply data for April sometime this session or on Thursday, and analysts expect the growth to slow somewhat from March's 8.3 percent rate.
But even if M3 were to show a decline in growth to the 7.6 percent average expectation, analysts said the data were unlikely to have much impact on Bunds.
"We know the Bundesbank will not move rates on the back of this, so the market will not take much notice as long as it's broadly in line with forecasts," said one Frankfurt-based trader.

This limited impact, coupled with a negative drag from domestic worries, will cap the June future's gains to around 102.00 for this session, traders said, adding that this level must be conquered before Bunds can make a good break higher.
